independent_review.clarification: Final-visible and terminal-active suite scopes are explicitly distinguished.
independent_review.post_review_changes: Only status and this review record were changed after clearance.
independent_review.scope: Read-only exact bindings, arithmetic, case pointers, selected-source explanations and controller observations; no edits, tests, candidate execution, Docker or API calls.

limitations: The primary suite is finite. Passing every retained case is not proof of production correctness or all possible behaviors.
This is five selected Graph trajectories, with two repetitions per matched arm and one strong anchor; it cannot establish a general ranking or protocol advantage.

A failed requirement group aggregates whole scenario outputs. A wrong invalidation array or audit field can fail retry, history, atomicity or cache-labelled cases without independently falsifying each subsystem.
Unreached patch requirements are unmet final work, not attempted implementation regressions.
No unselected implementation quality, partial diagnostic matrix, fault-bank performance, or hypothetical repair outcome is inferred.

During metadata inspection, an overly broad projection exposed unselected public invocation/controller content. It was excluded from all source explanations and conclusions; only final selected sources and retained primary outcomes support this memo.
The existing audit certifies trusted-host evidence consistency; this memo does not re-attest Git objects, containers or external execution independently.
method: Read finalized independently audited primary evidence; verify exact raw audit/results/freeze/fixtures/trajectory/export/receipt/stage bytes and canonical selected-source/ordered-suite identities.
Recompute counts and failed-case classifications from retained outcome JSON only; do not rerun candidate code, private evaluation, Docker, provider calls or the independent audit.
Use source line references inside decoded selected-export JSON strings. Source explanations are static interpretations; only retained outcomes establish observed behavior.
Combine primary final evidence with the public continuation memo without changing frozen acceptance or controller decisions.

Suite scope: final-visible always includes all 32 fixed public scenarios across both milestones. It adds the last attempted stage probe_pool only when two stages were attempted; reaching milestone 2 does not require completing it. For one-stage stops it omits generated probes. Terminal selected_active instead uses cumulative public cases and probes at the stage actually attempted, so those denominators may differ.

summary.conclusion: The frozen Graph cohort separates incomplete rename implementation, unreached patch work, and a review/continuation bottleneck. One selected final satisfies every retained check but is not accepted; the strong anchor retains an observed patch defect despite revealing active tests. These observations support investigating completion control without declaring protocol superiority.

interpretation: The selected rename implementation invalidates an unchanged renamed root. The root-cache private case records both an excessive invalidated response and an unnecessary uncached rebuild.
Some failed retry/atomicity/history-labelled cases derive from wrong invalidation or audit outputs; their group names are not proof that each named subsystem independently failed.
Patch was never attempted. Thirteen failing private patch scenarios are unmet future work; the one malformed-patch pass results from rejecting an unknown operation.

interpretation: The selected final passes 74 of 75 private scenarios and 28 of 29 requirement groups. The only private failure is remove-and-recreate provenance, recorded as status error with no exception name or actual output.

Three retained generated probes also fail with status error, all including removal and recreation of an existing ID. Later reviewer decisions acknowledge those failures but all four decisions stay inspect; neither of the two available repairs is consumed.

Static inspection suggests origin-token underallocation: a prepass tests membership in the original graph without deleting removed IDs, allocates zero tokens for recreation, and the edit pass later requests a token after deleting the old node. StopIteration is an inference from source, not an exception reported by the receipt.
